findings: Original POSIX FileId header uses stat and device+inode equality. Native macOS synthetic temporary-file controls verify hardlink equality, symlink target equality and missing-path invalidity. This supports scanner visited-ID behavior only when duplicate-inode suppression is enabled; no directory-cycle traversal tested.

Windows FileId compares volume serial and high/low file index, opens with GENERIC_READ and FILE_SHARE_READ, closes handle. Open failure yields invalid ID, which scanner does not insert in visited set. Windows behavior and junction resolution not executed.

writeFileAtomically writes a temporary file, removes existing destination and then renames temporary to destination. A crash/rename failure after removal can lose the original target; no fsync or verified replacement transaction visible. Name/doc promise alone does not prove crash safety. No real destination deletion/fault injection performed.

fullMd5 uses a dedicated producer pool, queue depth2 and128KiB chunks. It checks atEnd but does not propagate explicit read-error status/byte-total/source-stamp; stalled/error device behavior not executed. Scanner calling this helper is not proof of a stable full snapshot.

QCancelableIODevice readData returns-1 on cancellation; wrapped reads/seeks are delegated. Caller policy remains important because EOF/error/cancellation may otherwise be collapsed. SVG exclusion previously noted. No real decoder cancellation run.

loadMap reads key/value without checking read counts before insertion, so truncated records are not explicitly rejected at this helper. loadBinaryData compressed path returns qUncompress output without distinct decompression-error state; uncompressed path checks full size. No malformed native input executed.

SimpleIO_QFile readline copies returned bytes without adding a null terminator, contradicting always-null-terminated header contract. Stdio readline only writes null at maxLen-1, not immediately after an earlier newline. Source contract observations; call-site consequences incomplete.
saveBinaryData narrows uint64 len to int for fromRawData; admissible producer limits not yet audited. No huge allocation attempted.
